whoItFits.heading: When Austin SBA loan resource pages tend to fit
items: You operate a business in Greater Austin (Travis, Williamson, Hays, or Bastrop counties) and want local SBA district office details.
You want free local advisory support from the Texas State University SBDC before submitting financial documentation to lenders.
You are organizing a technology startup, commercial expansion, or acquisition project in Central Texas.
You want to connect local Austin advisory contacts with Fund44's clean national financing explainers.

whenItMayNotFit.heading: When this path may not fit as well
items: If you already know your exact loan structure (e.g. SBA 504 vs 7(a)), starting directly on national product pages is faster.
If your business is located in San Antonio or Dallas, review those specific metro resource pages instead.
If you require city-specific municipal permit or tax advice, consult the City of Austin or Travis County clerk directly.

commonQuestions.question: Which SBA district office covers Austin?
commonQuestions.answer: The SBA San Antonio District Office serves Austin and surrounding Travis, Williamson, and Hays counties.

commonQuestions.question: Where can I get free SBA loan application help in Austin?
commonQuestions.answer: The Texas State University SBDC provides free business consulting and loan prep assistance for Austin-area businesses.

commonQuestions.question: What is the difference between SBA 7(a) and 504 loans for Austin businesses?
commonQuestions.answer: SBA 7(a) offers up to $5M for general working capital, debt refinance, or acquisitions. SBA 504 is specialized for commercial real estate.

commonQuestions.question: Does Fund44 issue SBA loans directly in Austin?
commonQuestions.answer: No. Fund44 is an educational technology marketplace, not a lender. Loans are issued by third-party SBA participating lenders.
